title: Polymarket Halted International Trading After Hackers Drained Accounts
summary:
Trading has resumed on Polymarket’s flagship international platform after a hack that drained money from the wallets of some traders.
Polymarket declined to comment when WIRED asked how many traders were impacted by the breach and how much money was lost, but the company said it will refund impacted traders.
The hack did not impact users on Polymarket US, the company’s newer platform for people within the United States.
This is not the first time that Polymarket traders have experienced security woes.
In June 2026, Polymarket experienced another breach, which resulted in over $2 million in losses for impacted traders.

title: Neighbours: AI micro-drama recut of Australian show focusing on Margot Robbie worries actors and crew
summary:
Former Neighbours actors and crew have raised concerns about plans to use AI to help re-edit old footage and make mini episodes for mobile phone viewers.
Footage of Margot Robbie, who played Donna Freedman from 2008 to 2011, will be the initial focus of the micro-drama.
The micro-drama episodes will use "original, previously broadcast footage, dialogue and performances", according to Fremantle spokesman.
Using AI to help make short episodes from old footage was "like cutting up a Picasso and rebuilding it".

title: Apple’s new laptop supports one of the coolest features for color pros
summary:
It’s the first laptop, and only the second product overall, to support Apple CMF 2026 color modes.
The specification that’s been the standard for years is CIE 1931 (CIE stands for Commission Internationale de l’Éclairage, or International Commission on Illumination).
CIE 1931 doesn’t properly handle that and was created based on only 17 test subjects.
Apple CMF 2026 addresses that, so that displays look the same regardless of the technology they use.
Color science and display technologies have come a long way since 1931, when the CIE 1931 color space was established.

title: AI coding startup Cognition is weighing a new funding round at a $70 billion to $80 billion valuation
summary:
Just weeks after announcing a new round of funding at a $48 billion valuation, AI coding startup Cognition is fielding new investor interest at a much higher price.
The startup has received offers valuing it at between $70 billion and $80 billion and is seriously considering a round before the end of the year, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Founded in 2023 by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan, Cognition is best known for Devin, an AI coding agent designed to automate software engineering tasks.
Cognition's rapid valuation climb underscores the investor frenzy around AI coding, one of the hottest and most competitive corners of the AI market.
A $75 billion valuation wouldn't be so far-fetched, as SpaceX just acquired fellow AI coding giant Cursor for $60 billion a few months ago.

summary:

Announced Wednesday and available for purchase now, they include the Echo Dot ($100), Echo Studio With Home Camera ($250), Echo Show 16 ($500), Echo Time ($200), and the first Alexa Photo Frame ($200).
That’s higher than the marked-up prices on existing Amazon devices from this summer, which the company blamed on the memory shortage.

title: Amazon’s AI shopping assistant can now edit your grocery lists and gift registries
summary:
Is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more.
Amazon is adding several new features to its AI shopping assistant, including ways to create, edit, and move items between shopping lists and gift registries.
As an example, Amazon says you can now ask Alexa for Shopping to “Create a new shopping list” or “Show me what’s left on my wedding registry.”The ecommerce giant has continued to expand on its Alexa for Shopping assistant since its official launch in May, while resisting third-party AI shopping agents from companies like Meta and Perplexity.
Alexa for Shopping lives next to the search bar across Amazon’s app and website, and can do things like set price alerts, compare items, and automatically purchase products when they drop below a set price.
Along with the ability to manage registries and lists, Alexa for Shopping can now update your delivery instructions, answer billing questions about unrecognized charges and refunds, as well as pause and change recurring deliveries.

title: Barry Diller talks career pivots, AI in media, and MGM deal
summary:
Media titan Barry Diller, the chairman of publishing empire IAC, has built and rebuilt his career more than most executives, from network television to Hollywood studios to the earliest internet empires.
As part of Business Insider's The Long Play, Diller talked to Peter Kafka, Business Insider's chief correspondent covering media and technology, about what successful businesses require: good timing, nerve, and the willingness to walk away from what's working.
During this conversation, titled "The Art of the Comeback: A Masterclass on Resilience," Diller shares his perspectives on AI adoption.
He also talks about why his MGM Resorts deal fell apart and how he's leveraging legacy print publications like Southern Living to create new revenue streams.
The 84-year-old media and tech exec told Kafka he wants to keep working as long as he can be engaged and useful.
